title: Freya and the Homecoming
premise: Xanthe Nakamura has spent two years building 'Freya,' an anonymous online account that exposes the small cruelties of her elite prep school — until her coding teacher pairs her with Priya Raghavan, the girl whose life Freya's posts once dismantled, for a semester project neither can refuse. As they build a championship-winning app together, Xanthe discovers Priya has been quietly investigating Freya too, and that a school administrator is using the account's archive to cover up an older, darker incident. To save Priya and herself, Xanthe must unmask Freya publicly at the national competition, trading her invisibility for a justice the school will never grant — and discovering that being known was the thing she feared and needed most.
about_author: Ines Delacroix is a former debate coach who writes stories about teenagers who refuse to play by the rules adults wrote for them. She lives in Portland with a rescue greyhound and an unhealthy collection of mechanical keyboards.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We meet her double life: quiet coder by day, anonymous truth-teller 'Freya' by night, posting receipts about Westfield Prep's bullies. A new post about a stolen scholarship essay goes viral. Emotional beat: the thrill of power shadowed by loneliness — she helps everyone and knows no one.

chapters.title: The Pairing
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Mr. Okafor announces semester-long pairs for the state app championship: Xanthe with Priya Raghavan, whose reputation Freya destroyed last year when posts outed her family's financial aid. Priya's cold fury meets Xanthe's guilty silence. Emotional beat: dread; the mask has a crack in it.

chapters.title: Ground Rules
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The girls negotiate a truce over burnt coffee: professional only, no questions about the past. They brainstorm an app idea — a platform for reporting harassment anonymously. Irony thick enough to taste. Emotional beat: wary respect flickering under hostility.

chapters.title: What Freya Knows
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Late-night coding session reveals Priya is brilliant and funny, complicating everything. Meanwhile Freya receives a chilling DM from someone claiming to know who runs the account. Emotional beat: first real fear — the hunter sensing a hunter.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya admits she's spent a year trying to identify Freya — not for revenge, but because the posts about her were accurate in ways only an insider could know. She suspects someone fed Freya information. Emotional beat: Xanthe realizes Priya isn't the enemy; someone else is.

chapters.title: Vice Principal Voss
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Administrator Dean Voss summons both girls, suspiciously knowledgeable about their project, and warns them to drop 'distracting extracurriculars.' Xanthe notices Voss's office contains printouts of Freya's posts. Emotional beat: paranoia blooms; the adult world is not neutral.

chapters.title: Prototype
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The app — called Homecoming — takes shape, letting students document incidents with timestamped, encrypted evidence. Beta testers love it. First hackathon qualifier won. Emotional beat: joy of creation shared, the closest thing to friendship either has felt in years.

chapters.title: The DMs
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The mysterious messenger escalates: they claim Voss buried an incident years ago involving a beloved teacher, and that Freya's early posts touched it without knowing. They want Xanthe to dig. Emotional beat: vertigo — her weapon may have been aimed by someone else.

chapters.title: Old Yearbooks
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Library digging uncovers a withdrawn student, Marcus Hale, who left mid-year four years ago after an 'incident' never named. Voss signed his exit paperwork. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger; the school's polished memory has rot beneath.

chapters.title: Almost Friends
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A sleepover coding marathon; Priya talks about her father's deportation fight, why the scholarship posts cut so deep. Xanthe nearly confesses everything and doesn't. Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into guilt — every kind moment is built on her lie.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Someone leaks Homecoming's beta data to Voss, who moves to shut the project down as a 'privacy risk.' The anonymous messenger claims credit, forcing the girls' hand: finish it fast or lose it forever. Emotional beat: betrayal and urgency; the clock starts.

chapters.title: State Semifinals
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Against Voss's objections, they compete and advance, live on school streams. Voss publicly congratulates them while privately threatening expulsion over 'unauthorized data collection.' Emotional beat: defiant triumph with a blade behind it.

chapters.title: Marcus
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Tracking down Marcus Hale, now working at a garage two towns over, Xanthe hears the truth: Voss covered up hazing that injured him, protecting donors' sons. He begs her not to reopen it. Emotional beat: moral weight — justice might hurt the person it's meant to honor.

chapters.title: The Messenger Unmasked
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Xanthe traces the DMs: it's Mr. Okafor, the teacher, Marcus's cousin, who used Freya's fame hoping she'd finish what he couldn't. He apologizes but won't stop pushing. Emotional beat: anger and recognition — she's been a pawn, and pawns can choose.

chapters.title: Confession Interrupted
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe finally tells Priya she's Freya. Before Priya can respond, Voss bursts in with screenshots of Freya's posts traced to the school's network — Xanthe's IP — threatening criminal charges unless the account dies and Homecoming with it. Emotional beat: devastation; the truth arrives at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Silence
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya goes dark, processing: the app they built together is the same weapon that broke her. She finds, though, that Freya's original post about her was the only thing that ever made the school address the bullying. Emotional beat: painful reckoning — anger and gratitude tangled.

chapters.title: The Deal
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Voss offers terms: delete Freya, withdraw from nationals, silence about Marcus, and all records vanish. Xanthe pretends to accept while backing up everything to distributed servers. Emotional beat: cold clarity; she knows exactly what she's about to do.

chapters.title: Nationals
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Priya shows up anyway — 'we didn't build it for them.' On stage before judges and cameras, presenting Homecoming, Xanthe goes off-script: she unmasks herself as Freya and tells Marcus's story with the archived evidence, live. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into freedom.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The fallout detonates: Voss suspended pending investigation, local news everywhere, classmates split between gratitude and fury. Priya stands beside Xanthe publicly — forgiveness not granted cheaply, but chosen. Emotional beat: costly reconciliation.

chapters.title: Hearings
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. School board hearing where Marcus testifies, voice shaking, backed by Homecoming's timestamped records — the app vindicated as exactly what schools claim they want. Xanthe faces consequences for her methods even as her targets fall. Emotional beat: justice outside the law is messy and real.

chapters.title: The Last Post
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Freya signs off with a final post: the full archive, open-sourced, handed to the student body. Identity revealed, the mask retired. Priya and Xanthe plan what Homecoming could become beyond one school. Emotional beat: mourning the anonymity that kept her safe, embracing the self that remains.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Months later: nationals trophy on a shelf neither cares about, a new semester, a new pair of students asking Xanthe how to speak up safely. At the homecoming dance, present and accounted for, Xanthe dances with friends who know her name. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not hidden for.
